fair_value.method: Blend of three methods on 3.95B shares: SOTP ~$295 (60% weight), NTM P/E at the horizon ~$299 (30%), and 2027 consensus EPS $2.17 x 120 = $260 (10%), which gives ~$293, rounded to $295. The SOTP is auto $60 + energy $19 + FSD software $28 + probability-weighted robotaxi $115 + Optimus $65 + net cash/SpaceX stake $8. Robotaxi and FSD are trimmed for the NHTSA Special Order and the EU vote slipping to December.

methods.name: Sum of the parts
methods.detail: 3.95B shares. Core auto: ~$120B 2027 revenue x ~6% normalized net margin = ~$7B x 30 = ~$240B ($60/sh). Energy storage: ~$3B EBIT x 25 = ~$75B ($19/sh). FSD software: ~$110B ($28/sh), trimmed from $120B because EU-wide approval has slipped to December at the earliest with only 7 of 27 states. Robotaxi network, probability-weighted: ~$455B ($115/sh), trimmed from $500B because the NHTSA Special Order over FMVSS 135 (foot brake) could force a Part 555 exemption path and delay Cybercab scaling. Optimus, probability-weighted: ~$255B ($65/sh). Net cash $27.4B plus the SpaceX stake: ~$30B ($8/sh). Total ~$295.

methods.name: Forward P/E at horizon (NTM EPS in Sep 2027)
methods.detail: In Sept 2027 the market will price NTM EPS, a blend of 2027 ($2.17 consensus) and 2028 (~$2.85 assuming ~30% growth as capex-heavy autonomy spend begins to earn), so ~$2.60. At 115x, a premium multiple that is slightly compressed from today's ~171x on 2027 EPS as growth narrative is tested, that gives ~$299.

methods.name: 2027 consensus EPS x multiple (cross-check)
methods.detail: $2.17 (StockAnalysis, 2026-09-24) x 120x = $260. This corrects my round-1 cross-check, which used $2.68 and gave $320.

bear.story: NHTSA's Special Order leads to a Cybercab sales/operations pause or a forced Part 555 exemption process. The EU vote fails or keeps slipping. Capex above $25B/yr keeps FCF negative through 2027, funded by the up-to-$30B debt facilities. Auto margins slide as credits disappear and competition bites. 2027 EPS comes in under $2 and the multiple compresses toward 80-100x.

base.story: Deliveries grow modestly (~1.8-1.9M in 2027) and energy keeps growing. Cybercab gets through the NHTSA process with modest delay (a fix, exemption or limited operations). Robotaxi reaches several more states, though fewer than Musk's ~12 by year-end 2026 target. EU approval arrives in 2027 via a qualified majority or more national recognitions. FCF approaches breakeven by late 2027, and the stock trades a bit below spot, still carried by autonomy optionality.

bull.story: The NHTSA issue is resolved quickly. Unsupervised robotaxi scales to many states with thousands of Cybercabs, FSD wins EU and China approval, and Optimus shows external deployments. A SpaceX combination or the AI narrative re-rates the stock back above its $498 high.

thesis_break_reason: About 29% below the current price, and clearly under the $297 52-week low and the ~$304 July capitulation low, which already priced a 1.4% operating margin and negative FCF. A sustained trade there would most likely mean the autonomy thesis is damaged (NHTSA forcing a Cybercab pause or exemption process, a serious robotaxi incident, the unsupervised expansion stalling, EU/China FSD rejection) or core auto has turned loss-making while capex above $25B/yr continues. It would not be ordinary 46%-vol noise. I keep $265 rather than the supervisor's $258 because a close below the July low with no fresh fundamental news is already hard to explain as noise; the difference is small.

key_uncertainties: Outcome of the NHTSA Special Order: whether the Cybercab's lack of a foot brake (FMVSS 135) forces a pause or a Zoox-style Part 555 exemption process that delays scaling
Pace of unsupervised robotaxi expansion beyond ~200 vehicles in TX/FL/CA metros, against the ~12-state year-end target
How long FCF stays negative with capex above $25B/yr and up to $30B of debt capacity, and whether auto margins keep falling
Timing of EU-wide approval (December at the earliest, 7 of 27 states so far) and of China FSD approval
Tesla-SpaceX merger: roughly a coin flip before the horizon, with price effect of unclear sign
Valuation regime: ~171x 2027 consensus EPS leaves the stock very sensitive to narrative and rates
reasoning: Round 2 revision. The supervisor's fact checks all verified, and I accept all of them. (1) 2027 consensus EPS is $2.17, not $2.68, so my 120x cross-check falls from $320 to $260 and the stock trades at ~171x 2027. (2) The EU vote is not on Oct 6: the TCMV agenda has discussion only, and December is the earliest vote, with 7 of 27 states on board. (3) NHTSA escalated to a Special Order on Sept 10 with a sworn response due Sept 30. The fine is immaterial, but FMVSS 135 non-compliance could force a pause or exemption route, which is a near-term left-tail risk. (4) My 80-90% merger odds were too high: Polymarket has ~18% for a 2026 announcement and ~54% by mid-2027, and the sign of any price effect is unclear, so I no longer fatten the right tail for it. My share count (3.95B) was already correct. I rebuilt fair value as a blend: SOTP $295 (robotaxi trimmed to $115/sh and FSD software to $28/sh), NTM P/E at horizon ~$299 (~$2.60 x 115x), and 2027 EPS x 120 = $260, weighted 60/30/10 to ~$295 (from $320). That is ~21% below spot. Like round 1, I do not expect fundamental value to bind within 12 months, because TSLA trades on autonomy narrative and analyst targets average ~$397 (median $415). So I moved the median only from ~$365 to ~$355. I kept sigma at ~0.50 because the binary events (NHTSA, state expansion, EU vote, merger) justify tails wider than the 46% realized vol. I removed some of the merger-driven right-tail fattening but kept a slight fat right tail for TSLA's history of narrative re-ratings. Scenarios: bear $210 at 27%, base $350 at 50%, bull $580 at 23%, for a mean of ~$365. The ladder gives P(>=372) = 0.465 (from 0.49) and P(>=502) = 0.245 (from 0.26). Research was ~5 additional web searches; no options data consulted and nothing under priors/ opened.
